questions.stem: Which of the following is an example of a public enterprise in Nigeria?
questions.explanation: The Nigerian National Petroleum Corporation (NNPC) is a government-owned enterprise, making it a public enterprise. The other options are privately owned companies.

distractorRationale.a: Dangote Cement is a private company focused on cement production.
distractorRationale.b: MTN Nigeria is a private telecommunications company.
distractorRationale.c: Nestle Nigeria is a private food and beverage company.

questions.stem: What is the primary goal of privatisation?

options.text: To increase government control over businesses

questions.explanation: The primary goal of privatisation is to improve efficiency and profitability by transferring ownership to the private sector. This often leads to better management and innovation.

distractorRationale.a: Privatisation reduces government control, rather than increasing it.
distractorRationale.b: Privatisation does not aim to eliminate competition; it often encourages it.
distractorRationale.c: While privatisation may affect jobs, its main goal is not to reduce public service jobs.

questions.stem: Which of the following is NOT a feature of cooperative societies?
questions.explanation: Cooperative societies focus on mutual benefit rather than profit maximization for owners. They are designed to serve the interests of their members.

distractorRationale.a: Democratic control is a key feature of cooperatives, allowing members to participate in decision-making.
distractorRationale.b: Voluntary membership is fundamental to cooperatives, as individuals join freely.
distractorRationale.c: Mutual benefit is the core objective of cooperative societies, ensuring all members gain from their participation.
